simple.meaning: מַדָּע (maddâʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “intelligence or consciousness.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H4093. madda מַדָּע noun masculine 2Chr 1:12 knowledge, thought (late); מַדָּע 1:10 4 t.; מִדָּֽעֲךָ Eccl 10:20 ; — 1 knowledge (|| חָכְמָה ) of Solomon, 2Chr 1:10-11 , 12 ; Dan 1:4 (|| חָכְמָה and דַּעַת ), 1:7 (|| הַשְׂכֵּל ). 2 place of knowledge, mind , (in our idiom also) thought Eccl 10:20 .

occurrences.englishText: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”

God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you, nor yet have you asked for long life; but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king,
therefore wisdom and knowledge is granted to you. I will give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had who have been before you had, and none after you will have.”
Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts;

youths in whom was no defect, but well-favored, and skillful in all wisdom, and endowed with knowledge, and understanding science, and who had the ability to stand in the king’s palace; and that he should teach them the learning and the language of the Chaldeans.
Now as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
